questions.q: Which three tables directly extend task?
options: sys_user, sys_dictionary, sys_db_object
cmdb_ci, sc_catalog, kb_knowledge
incident, problem, change_request
sc_request, sc_req_item, sys_id
questions.explain: incident, problem, and change_request each extend task directly, inheriting its fields and shared logic.

questions.q: How does the Service Catalog's request structure relate to task?
options: sc_req_item extends task directly, and sc_request extends sc_req_item
sc_request extends task, and sc_req_item extends sc_request — so both are task records through two levels of extension
sc_request and sc_req_item have no relationship to task at all
Only sc_req_item exists; sc_request is not a real table
questions.explain: sc_request extends task, and the individual requested items (sc_req_item) extend sc_request — a two-level hierarchy under task.

questions.q: Why did Incident, Problem, and Change Management (from Course 1) feel so similar to administer in ServiceNow?
options: They are all stored in sys_dictionary instead of being real tables
ServiceNow renames the same table depending on which application menu you use
They don't actually share any technical structure, only similar names
All three extend the same base table, task, so shared logic like state and priority calculation is defined once
questions.explain: Incident, problem, and change_request all extend task, so the shared lifecycle and priority logic lives once on the base table.

questions.q: A single laptop order through the Service Catalog produces which records?
options: Only a single incident record
A single change_request covering the whole order
Only a sys_dictionary entry describing the laptop
One sc_request for the overall order and one sc_req_item for the specific laptop line item
questions.explain: The overall order is an sc_request; each individual item within it (like the laptop) is a separate sc_req_item.

questions.q: How can you tell whether a field is shared platform-wide across the task hierarchy versus specific to one branch?
options: Check whether the field exists on task itself — if it does, every table extending task shares it; if not, it's specific to that branch
All fields on every table are always shared, with no exceptions
Field sharing is random and cannot be determined
Only fields starting with sys_ can ever be shared
questions.explain: A field defined on task is inherited by every table that extends it; a field defined only on a child table (like caller_id on incident) is specific to that branch.
